title: Role of Atom Probe Tomography in Sustainable Materials Recycling and Design
content: Atom Probe Tomography (APT) serves as a pivotal technique in the sustainable recycling of materials, offering unparalleled atomic-scale insights into impurity incorporation, dopant retention, and microstructural evolution. In recycled materials, residual impurities and additive elements play a dual role, they can either enhance or degrade properties such as mechanical strength, thermal stability, and electrical performance. The redistribution and clustering of these species can significantly impact alloy phase stability, grain boundary cohesion, and functional characteristics. Understanding and controlling these effects is crucial for optimizing recycling strategies and ensuring material performance in secondary applications. APT, alongside complementary electron microscopy (EM) enables precise characterization of impurity behavior. While EM provides nanostructural chemical mapping and offers phase distribution analysis, APT uniquely delivers three-dimensional atomic-scale composition profiling, revealing segregation and clustering phenomena with sub-nanometer precision. This information is critical for designing next-generation recycled materials with tailored properties, mitigating impurity-driven embrittlement, and enabling performance optimization. By integrating APT with advanced microscopy and materials informatics, researchers can push the boundaries of circular materials design, fostering a new era of high-performance, resource-efficient alloys and functional materials in a circular economy framework. Here, this presentation will highlight the transformative role of APT in recycled materials design, showcasing its potential to drive innovation in sustainable metallurgy and advanced materials engineering.
